quizName: DMV Practice Test #9 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What does a solid white line on the side of the road mean?

options.text: Parking is not allowed.
The right edge of the traffic lane.
Traffic must merge.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right edge of the traffic lane.
questions.explanation: A solid white line on the side of the road marks the right edge of the traffic lane.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, what should you do?

options.text: Avoid sudden movements to prevent skidding.
Ride on the shoulder to stay out of traffic.
Use only the rear brake because the front brake does not work well on slippery surfaces.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid sudden movements to prevent skidding.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, any sudden change in speed, direction, gear, or braking can cause a skid. Make all movements smooth and gradual.

questions.question: How does improper braking affect motorcycle safety?

options.text: It usually causes no problems.
It is a major cause of motorcycle crashes.
It is not a concern because motorcycles have two brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is a major cause of motorcycle crashes.
questions.explanation: Improper braking causes many motorcycle crashes. Using correct braking technique is essential for safe riding.

questions.question: You see an emergency vehicle stopped on the side of the road with its lights flashing. What should you do?

options.text: Stop behind the emergency vehicle on the roadway.
Stop and wait for the emergency vehicle to move.
Move to another lane away from the emergency vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to another lane away from the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: When you approach a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights, change lanes to give it extra space. Slow down and be ready to stop at all emergency scenes.

questions.question: Which brake on a motorcycle is more powerful?

options.text: The front brake
The rear brake
Both brakes are equally powerful.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front brake
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful and provides at least 70 percent of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: When should you wear hearing protection while riding?

options.text: Not needed when wearing a helmet.
Only on long trips.
On every ride.

questions.correctAnswerText: On every ride.
questions.explanation: Engine and wind noise can damage your hearing, even with a helmet. Wear hearing protection on all rides.

questions.question: When riding behind another vehicle at night, how can you tell if there are bumps in the road ahead?

options.text: Listen for the vehicle scraping the pavement.
Watch the other vehicle's taillights bouncing up and down.
Look at the rear bumper to see if it is bouncing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch the other vehicle's taillights bouncing up and down.
questions.explanation: Watch the vehicle ahead of you to see road conditions. If its taillights bounce up and down, there are bumps in the road ahead.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, should you move to the far side of your lane?

options.text: Yes, because you will be farther from the passing vehicle.
No, because it signals the other driver to move back into your lane too early.
It does not matter because it has no effect on safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, because it signals the other driver to move back into your lane too early.
questions.explanation: Do not move to the far side of your lane when being passed. This may cause the passing driver to return to your lane too soon.

questions.question: How are traffic lanes going in the same direction separated?

options.text: By white lines.
By yellow lines.
By road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: By white lines.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. Solid white lines mean no passing. Dashed white lines mean passing is allowed if it is safe.

questions.question: Where is the greatest risk of conflict between you and other vehicles?

options.text: At an intersection
On the highway
On any road

questions.correctAnswerText: At an intersection
questions.explanation: Intersections are where motorcycles face the greatest risk of conflict with other vehicles.

questions.question: One problem with riding a motorcycle next to another vehicle is that:

options.text: The other vehicle may block your escape route.
Other drivers can easily see the motorcycle.
The rider may not be able to read road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: The other vehicle may block your escape route.
questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous. The vehicle could move into your lane and hit you. It could also block your escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: If you are in a collision, you must tell law enforcement if there is:

options.text: An injury.
Death.
Property damage of more than $1,000.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: In Wyoming, you must report a collision to authorities if it results in an injury, death, or property damage of $1,000 or more.

questions.question: As you drink more alcohol, your ability to safely ride:

options.text: Improves.
Stays the same.
Gets worse.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gets worse.
questions.explanation: Alcohol decreases the skills you need to ride safely. Any amount of alcohol makes riding more dangerous. Do not ride if you have consumed any alcohol.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, a motorcycle rider has an advantage because:

options.text: The motorcycle can speed up faster than a car.
The rider can position the motorcycle on the left side of the lane to avoid people and cars on the right.
Motorcycles stop shorter than cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: The rider can position the motorcycle on the left side of the lane to avoid people and cars on the right.
questions.explanation: When passing parked cars on your right, you can ride on the left side of your lane. This helps you avoid opening doors, people getting out, or people stepping between cars. Only do this if there is no oncoming traffic.

questions.question: How are convex mirrors different from flat mirrors?

options.text: They show a narrower view of the road.
They show a wider view of the road.
They show a clearer view of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They show a wider view of the road.
questions.explanation: Many motorcycles have convex mirrors. Compared to flat mirrors, they show a wider view. However, they can also make vehicles appear farther away than they really are.

questions.question: To help others see your motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Use your headlight only at night or in poor visibility.
Always use your headlight.
Add an orange tint to your headlight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use your headlight.
questions.explanation: Using your headlight at all times is the best way to help others see your motorcycle.

questions.question: Stopping while turning is difficult because:

options.text: The bike is leaning, so there is less grip available for stopping.
The rider is focused on the turn, not on braking.
The brakes do not work when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: The bike is leaning, so there is less grip available for stopping.
questions.explanation: You can use both brakes while turning, but you must be very careful. When the motorcycle is leaning, some grip is used for the turn. This leaves less grip for stopping.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT help reduce serious injury in a crash:

options.text: A DOT-approved helmet.
A leather jacket.
A sweatshirt.

questions.correctAnswerText: A sweatshirt.
questions.explanation: A DOT-approved helmet protects your head and neck. A leather jacket or sturdy synthetic jacket also protects you. A sweatshirt does not provide adequate protection.

questions.question: "Stay-awake" pills:

options.text: Are a good way to stay awake on long trips.
Do not encourage risky behavior.
Usually have no side effects.
Make you feel alert even when you are not.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make you feel alert even when you are not.
questions.explanation: Artificial stimulants create a false feeling of alertness and may hide how tired you really are. It is dangerous to ride while using these pills.

questions.question: Taking over-the-counter medicine before riding:

options.text: Is usually fine because over-the-counter medicines are weak.
Is always acceptable.
May affect your riding and should be done carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: May affect your riding and should be done carefully.
questions.explanation: Many legal medicines, including over-the-counter drugs, can affect your ability to ride safely. Talk to your doctor about how any new medicine may affect your driving or riding.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT help you control a motorcycle in a turn?

options.text: Speed up through the turn.
Slow down before turning.
Lean into the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up through the turn.
questions.explanation: To stay in control during a turn, slow down before you enter it. Look ahead in the direction you want to go. Press the handle grip to lean the right way. Then gently roll the throttle through the turn to keep the suspension steady.

questions.question: Changing gears while in a curve:

options.text: Should only be done if you can do it smoothly.
Is better than changing gears before the curve.
Is the best way to control your speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should only be done if you can do it smoothly.
questions.explanation: It is best to change gears before you start turning. If you must change gears while turning, do it smoothly. A sudden change in power to the rear wheel can cause you to skid.

questions.question: Small vehicles look ________ and slower than they really are.

options.text: Closer
Farther away
Larger

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther away
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge how fast and how far away a small vehicle is, such as a motorcycle. Do not assume that drivers in large vehicles can judge your speed and location correctly.

questions.question: The faster you drink alcohol:

options.text: The faster your body removes it.
The faster it builds up in your body.
The less it affects your body.

questions.correctAnswerText: The faster it builds up in your body.
questions.explanation: The faster you drink, the faster alcohol builds up in your body. Your body removes about one drink per hour. If you drink more than one drink in an hour, alcohol will still be in your body after one hour.

questions.question: When sitting on a motorcycle, your arms should:

options.text: Have a large bend at the elbow when reaching for the handle grips.
Be slightly bent when holding the handle grips.
Be fully extended when reaching for the handle grips.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be slightly bent when holding the handle grips.
questions.explanation: Your arms should be slightly bent when holding the handle grips. Bent arms reduce tiredness and let you push on the handlebars without stretching.
